title: 2025-05-06 GPTQ/AWQ quant regression debug - VPC/onprem
summary: Redwood SE and Helios ML team debugged an accuracy regression observed after switching from GPTQ-4bit to AWQ/INT8 on a private VPC deployment. Main hypotheses: calibration dataset mismatch, per-channel vs per-tensor scales, KV-cache/batching interaction with quantized kernels. Agreed next steps include a controlled eval run (1k prompts) across FP16/GPTQ/AWQ with and without KV cache, share kernel logs and quant configs, and schedule a follow-up deep benchmark next week.
topics: INT8 vs FP8 vs GPTQ tradeoffs
VPC/on-prem kernel selection and libcudnn differences
action_items: Priya: run controlled eval (1k prompt set) for FP16/GPTQ/AWQ, capture per-prompt diffs and latency (due 2025-05-09)
Omar: pull quantization config and kernel selection logs from Dedicated node (share s3 link) (due 2025-05-08)
Maria: circulate internal note on rollback plan and pricing impact for FP16 fallback (due 2025-05-10)
next_steps: Helios to run eval and upload results to shared folder
Redwood to provide tuned AWQ presets and calibration script
Schedule follow-up 60-min call week of 2025-05-12 with expanded benchmark results
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maria Chen: Okay everyone we can get started. Thanks for making time, this is the rubric session to walk through the regression you're seeing after moving to AWQ int8 on your private cluster.
00:00:12 - Priya Shah: Hey thanks Maria, yeah quick context - we moved from a GPTQ-4bit rollout in staging to AWQ-int8 in our VPC and our instruction-following F1 dropped roughly 3 to 5%. Latency improved but user reported more hallucinations.
00:00:29 - Omar Ruiz: Hi, Omar from Redwood infra/SE. Can you clarify if that was perftest with KV cache on and continuous batching?
00:00:36 - Priya Shah: We had prefix caching turned on, yes. Batching was at our default 32 concurrency with dynamic batching window 40ms.
00:00:44 - Liam O'Sullivan: Also to note, our on-prem nodes are running CUDA 12.1 + custom libcudnn, so there might be kernel differences vs Redwood hosted.
00:00:54 - Maria Chen: Good call. That's exactly one of the hypotheses. We'll try to enumerate reasons: calibration mismatch, quantization granularity, kernel implementation difference, and KV-cache/batching interaction.
00:01:06 - Dr. Amit Rao: From an ops lens we need to know if rollback is straightforward and what impact on cost/throughput.
00:01:13 - Maria Chen: Totally. Omar, do you want to take us through the GPTQ vs AWQ tradeoffs quickly?
00:01:20 - Omar Ruiz: Sure. High level: GPTQ-style (our 4-bit setup) often reduces memory more aggressively and has lower accuracy regression if it's done per-channel with groupwise quantization and recalibration. AWQ/int8 is attractive for kernel-level speedups and commodity int8 paths, but it's sensitive to calibration dataset and activation distribution. AWQ can be asymmetric weight quant which sometimes shifts logits on rare tokens, which looks like hallucination.
00:01:50 - Priya Shah: Is that the same as what we saw when some of our rare-medical-terminology tokens spiked?
00:01:55 - Omar Ruiz: Yes, that matches. If the quant scales for some heads are off, the logits for low-frequency tokens can move unexpectedly. Also certain attention kernel rewrites for int8 can change softmax numerics.
00:02:07 - Maria Chen: We should log the per-head scale distributions. Priya, do you have the calibration corpuses used for AWQ?
00:02:14 - Priya Shah: We used a 100k-line clinical note dump + 10k synthetic prompts, but the distribution skew is more general English than your eval set which is very instruction-heavy.
00:02:24 - Omar Ruiz: There's a big smell there. PTQ calibration must reflect the inference distribution. If your eval set is instruction prompts, calibration on clinical notes drifts. That's our first suspicion.
00:02:35 - Liam O'Sullivan: Is retraining or quantization aware fine-tuning needed? We prefer not to do full QAT, but can we do lightweight calibration?
00:02:43 - Omar Ruiz: You can do a small calibration set matched to instruction style, or do MinMax vs MSE vs KL divergence collectives for per-channel scaling. AWQ tools we use support per-channel MSE cal which helps.
00:02:56 - Dr. Amit Rao: Another angle — could the KV cache cause divergence if cached KV tensors were generated under FP16 and later read under int8 runtime? Does Redwood convert caches?
00:03:06 - Omar Ruiz: Important point. In our runtime the KV cache is stored in the server memory in fp16 or bf16 depending on model cfg, and the quantized kernels read from dequantized activations on the fly. But if there's a mismatch in serialization format between your on-prem loader and Redwood runtime, you can see correctness errors.
00:03:23 - Priya Shah: We did see one off error where a cache checkpoint had NaNs after a restart. Might be unrelated but worth looking.
00:03:30 - Maria Chen: Ok, so action item to validate checkpoint serialization and a small canonical cache roundtrip test.
00:03:36 - 00:10:12 - [Transcript jump due to recording chunking]
00:10:13 - Omar Ruiz: Back to quant details — GPTQ 4-bit often uses per-channel scale + codebook compensation and can keep logits closer to fp16 baseline on common tokens. But it costs you runtime complexity: custom kernels, sometimes slower batched throughput if not fused. AWQ/int8 on modern kernels tends to be fastest for throughput but has those edge-case accuracy shifts.
00:10:40 - Priya Shah: So tradeoff is accuracy vs throughput. In our product, accuracy is critical for medical triage. Latency is secondary. So maybe we shouldn't have switched.
00:10:50 - Maria Chen: That helps prioritize. If accuracy trumps latency, rollback to GPTQ or FP16 fallback is safe. We'll quantify cost delta.
00:11:00 - Liam O'Sullivan: On the kernel side, we're running cuBLAS and custom fused attention kernels. Could Redwood's kernel selection be choosing a faster but numerically different kernel?
00:11:10 - Omar Ruiz: Yes. The runtime selects kernels based on sequence length heuristics and batch distribution. We can force kernel variants and reproduce your on-prem env. We'll provide a kernel selection dump.
00:11:21 - Priya Shah: What about batching interactions? We noticed regressions increase under burst traffic.
00:11:26 - Omar Ruiz: Continuous batching can change the effective sequence layout and how KV cache is reused. Some quantized kernels are pessimistic and saturate with certain batch sizes, causing different pad handling which can slightly change attention masks. That may amplify small quantization shifts.
00:11:42 - Maria Chen: Let's outline the prioritized experiments: 1) Controlled eval across FP16, GPTQ-4, AWQ-int8 with KV cache on/off; 2) Per-head scale histograms and per-token delta analysis; 3) Reproduce on a Redwood node with same CUDA/libcudnn; 4) Checkpoint serialization test.
00:11:58 - Priya Shah: Sounds good. For the controlled eval, how do you want us to structure prompts? We have a 10k production sample but could sample 1k representative ones.
00:12:07 - Omar Ruiz: Start with 1k: 300 instruction prompts, 300 clinical notes, 200 rare-token tests, 200 edge-case dialogue turns. We'll provide the template and a script to compute per-prompt accuracy and hallucination diff.
00:12:19 - Dr. Amit Rao: On the security side, we'll need your test harness to run within our VPC, so share the container and we can run it air-gapped.
00:12:26 - Maria Chen: We'll provide a signed container and the calibration script. It can run entirely in your VPC.
00:12:32 - 00:22:00 - [Long debug discussion; background talk about eval metrics and collection] 
00:22:01 - Priya Shah: We also tried FP8 experiments briefly—there's literature saying FP8 can be a middle ground. Did Redwood validate FP8 on the family of models we're using?
00:22:11 - Omar Ruiz: We have early FP8 support (E4M2/E5M2 variants). FP8 reduces memory and tends to preserve logits better than naive int8 in some workloads because it's floating point. But FP8 hardware support is limited; on your on-prem GPUs, fp8 kernels might not be optimized and can be slower than int8. Also toolchain maturity matters; we can run FP8 as a controlled test though.
00:22:36 - Liam O'Sullivan: Our nodes are Ampere A100s, FP8 would need newer drivers and libcudnn; OK we'll try.
00:22:43 - Maria Chen: Good. We'll include FP8 in the matrix but caveat performance expectations.
00:22:48 - Priya Shah: Another question — does PEFT / LoRA interfere with quantization? We have models fine-tuned with LoRA.
00:22:56 - Omar Ruiz: LoRA + quantization is generally fine if your adapter weights are kept in fp16 or merged carefully. Merged LoRA can amplify quantization error if you quantize merged weights without re-calibration. Preferred flow: quantize base model, then apply LoRA at inference if platform supports it, or merge and re-calibrate.
00:23:14 - Priya Shah: We merged LoRA into weights in our pipeline for simplicity. Maybe we need to re-quantize post-merge.
00:23:20 - Omar Ruiz: Exactly. That could be another source of shift.
00:23:25 - Maria Chen: We'll add a check: compare merged-vs-unmerged quant deltas.
00:23:29 - 00:34:00 - [Interruption for a terse network flake; recording continues]
00:34:02 - Omar Ruiz: Back — on numeric diffs, we'll compute per-token logit L2 and per-prompt top-1 token delta. Small average L2 but high delta on rare tokens indicates scale miscalibration.
00:34:20 - Priya Shah: We did an internal perplexity comparison — avg perplexity rose by 1.8 points post-AWQ. Is that large?
00:34:29 - Omar Ruiz: For instruction tasks, small perplexity changes can correspond to bigger behavior shifts. Perplexity is a useful signal but not definitive. Token-level agreement and human eval of hallucinations are critical.
00:34:40 - Maria Chen: For the human eval, we'll help construct a focused annotation rubric for hallucination scoring. We'll also suggest a threshold for rollback (e.g., >2.5% instruction-following delta).
00:34:54 - Liam O'Sullivan: About rollback plan — how hard is it to roll back traffic? Do you support model-level fallback routing?
00:35:01 - Omar Ruiz: Yes, Redwood routing supports canary and automatic fallback. We can set a policy to revert to GPTQ or FP16 if regression metrics cross a threshold. There is a short outage risk for in-flight requests but we can do staged switch.
00:35:12 - Priya Shah: That helps. We'd prefer automatic fallback if the regression is material.
00:35:18 - Maria Chen: We'll draft an SLO-based fallback policy and share.
00:35:22 - 00:46:00 - [Deep dive into kernel logs and instrumentation; Omar describes log collection] 
00:46:01 - Omar Ruiz: I'll outline the exact logs we need: kernel selection trace, per-layer quant scales, dequant buffers snapshot, and attention mask historian for a failed prompt. Also a short script to repro with pinned kernel variant.
00:46:18 - Priya Shah: We'll enable debug logs on a staging replica and attach them. Expect initial logs tomorrow.
00:46:25 - Maria Chen: Great. Omar, can you also provide AWQ preset files and a calibration script with options: per-channel MSE, per-tensor KL, symmetric vs asymmetric?
00:46:35 - Omar Ruiz: Yep. We'll include recommended presets: AWQ-default-int8, AWQ-int8-calibrated-instruction, and fallback GPTQ-4bit. We'll also add a small runner to run eval locally and produce per-prompt diffs.
00:46:48 - Priya Shah: For the eval runner, can it accept a cache on/off flag so we can see delta?
00:46:52 - Omar Ruiz: Yes, pass --kv-cache true/false.
00:46:56 - Dr. Amit Rao: One compliance note — any shared debug artifacts must exclude PHI. We'll mask and share only truncated token ids.
00:47:03 - Maria Chen: Absolutely. We'll provide scripts to strip sensitive content.
00:47:07 - 00:53:00 - [Negotiation of benchmarks and timeline] 
00:53:01 - Priya Shah: OK to recap what we all agreed?
00:53:04 - Maria Chen: Sure. Recap: 1) Helios runs 1k eval across FP16/GPTQ/AWQ (KV cache on/off); 2) Redwood provides AWQ presets, calibration scripts, kernel selection dump, and repro runner; 3) run checkpoint serialization test; 4) include FP8 in the matrix as an optional candidate; 5) set up follow-up call week of 2025-05-12.
00:53:28 - Priya Shah: Yes. We'll try to have results by 2025-05-09.
00:53:33 - Maria Chen: Great. Any final Qs?
00:53:36 - Liam O'Sullivan: One last micro question — is there a recommended min-batch size for AWQ int8 to avoid pad edge numerical issues?
00:53:43 - Omar Ruiz: We recommend grouping to avoid extreme padding: prefer batch sizes >8 and dynamic pad trimming. But we will test with your distribution.
00:53:55 - Dr. Amit Rao: Thanks all. This was productive.
00:53:59 - Maria Chen: Thanks team. We'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite.
00:54:05 - [Meeting ends]
notes: Be careful with calibration distribution; instruction-like prompts must be in calibration set
Consider FP16 fallback if accuracy constraints dominate
Check LoRA merge workflow before quantizing
